canonical_answers: Independent variable: ion speed v. Dependent variable: measured radius r of the circular path. Control: magnetic field strength and ion charge held fixed.

payload.text: A singly charged positive ion moves at 3.00×10⁵ m/s perpendicular to a uniform 0.200 T magnetic field.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Design a feasible measurement that tests the governing relation; identify the independent variable, dependent variable, and one control.

criteria.description: A feasible measurement design: vary the ion's speed (e.g., by changing an accelerating potential difference) and measure the resulting radius of its circular path in the field. Independent variable = ion speed v; dependent variable = measured radius r of the circular path; control = the magnetic field strength (0.200 T) and the ion's charge, held fixed across trials.
required_evidence: dependent variable: measured radius r of the circular path
control: magnetic field strength and ion charge held fixed
accepted_variants: Equivalent scientifically correct notation and reasoning earn credit.
criteria.minimum_fix: To earn this point, explicitly show independent variable: ion speed v; dependent variable: measured radius r of the circular path; control: magnetic field strength and ion charge held fixed.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain why assuming non-relativistic speeds and a uniform field lets you use qvB = mv²/r to solve for the radius, rather than needing relativistic corrections.

criteria.description: Explain why assuming non-relativistic speeds and a uniform field lets you use qvB = mv²/r to solve for the radius, rather than needing relativistic corrections.
accepted_variants: Equivalent scientifically correct notation and reasoning earn credit.
criteria.minimum_fix: To earn this point, explicitly show uniform magnetic field assumption; non-relativistic speed assumption.
